title: Slime Rancher: six faces and a separate mouth mask

people.name: Ian McConville
people.role: Principal Artist; author of the Slime Rancher 1.4.0 face-shader rebuild (the post spells the title 'Principle Artist')

summary: A developer-supplied six-face GIF shows how much expression can fit on the same nearly featureless round body.

observations.text: In the inspected GIF frame, the happy bottom-centre face uses dot eyes and a broad open mouth; the worried bottom-right face retains tiny eyes but replaces that mouth with a small downturned shape. The body design stays consistent.
The startled bottom-left face enlarges the eye marks and uses a small open mouth. This is an expression-shape comparison, not a verified timing analysis.

McConville describes separate eye and mouth channels in an RGBA distance-field mask, mouth-size changes through smoothstep, and UV noise for face wobble. He says swapping the source texture produces different faces.

mistIdeas: Our inference: keep MIST's familiar eyes and body, and author a small set of clearly different mouth silhouettes before adding more continuous movement.

Our inference: separate gaze, eye aperture, and mouth state so a listening response can move the eyes first and change the mouth only after recognition. The delayed timing is our proposal, not a measured property of this GIF.
Our inference: use wobble as a small secondary effect; it should not replace authored reactions or make every state equally active.

media.alt: Six pink slimes compare angry, distressed, altered-eye, startled, happy and worried face shapes.

sources.title: Slime Faces: Behind The Scenes, 25 June 2019
sources.supports: Named artist, face shader design, exact official GIF and its context.

title: Lil Gator Game: a heavy head with a simple face

people.name: Scott Slucher
people.role: Developer explaining his character design and animation implementation

summary: Slucher's own explanation separates authored movement, speed-dependent blending, head lag and secondary physics.

observations.text: The inspected sword-swing image puts the large pale eye and black pupil against the green head; the open jaw and broad head silhouette remain readable amid the flying cardboard. This is a still-image observation.
Slucher says the oversized head and arms make small movements read strongly; he accounts for the head's weight when animating.

Slucher describes blend trees driven by speed and surface angle, then procedural head lag and body leaning in turns. He explicitly says the blended animations are subtler, so large movements are not constant.

mistIdeas: Our inference: give MIST's eye/head orientation a small follow-through relative to a body turn, then let it settle cleanly.
Our inference: distinguish a quiet attention shift from a full-body enthusiastic response; do not reuse the same large bounce for both.
Our inference: test the expression in a frozen silhouette first. The face should remain readable before adding spring motion.

title: Psychonauts 2: Richardson's mailroom robot acting

people.name: Miyuki Richardson
people.role: Animator in official credits; reel author showing in-game animations, layouts and cutscenes

summary: A credited animator's reel offers a useful robot comparison and clearly labels her animation work separately from layout-only contributions.

observations.text: In the inspected mailroom sequence around 4:08 to 4:20, the robot's luminous circular eye, head angle, and oversized mechanical hand make the letter exchange readable. At 4:14 the frame places the eye beside the envelope, bringing face and task into one composition.

At approximately 4:20 the reel visibly labels the shot 'Layout and Animation'. Earlier examples, including the inspected 1:36 frame, say 'Layout Only' and credit final animation to Squeeze Animation Studios.
Double Fine's official credits name Richardson among the animators and separately acknowledge FaceFX-generated facial animations; this does not establish which mechanism any individual shot uses.

mistIdeas: Our inference: tie a MIST attention change to an actual event or object, then align the face, head, and one body gesture around that target.
Our inference: a mechanical face can retain its identity while the head and body carry emphasis. Avoid forcing a human mouth performance into every response.
Our inference: review future MIST animation in labelled stages: anticipation, attention shift, reaction hold, and return. The reel does not supply measured timing values for these stages.
